headline: Records persist as hike odds fade and earnings season opens
body: Major indices remain parked near record territory, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite both pushing toward fresh highs over the past week while the Dow lags behind, a pattern consistent with tech and AI-linked names still setting the pace. The backdrop is an unusual one: the Fed, under new chair Kevin Warsh, raised rates to a 3.75%-4.00% range in September -- its first hike since 2023 -- as inflation pressures tied to the escalation of the Iran conflict earlier this year complicated the policy picture even as equities kept climbing. Treasury yields have eased off the multi-year highs reached in the selloff that followed that move, and crude oil has retreated, a combination that has helped risk assets hold their gains heading into the start of bank-led earnings season.

The more consequential story underneath is how fast rate expectations have swung. A soft September jobs report -- just 29,000 payrolls added and unemployment ticking up to 4.2% -- knocked the odds of an October hike from roughly 70% down to the 20-25% range within days, and this week's FOMC minutes from the September meeting reportedly held no major surprises. Volatility has been historically subdued through the summer, though several outlets flagged the August-to-October stretch as seasonally shakier even amid the calm. Retail and social-media sentiment didn't surface anything distinct enough to flag today -- broader research suggests forums like WallStreetBets tend to react to market moves rather than lead them -- so this read leans primarily on price action and the rates repricing rather than social chatter.
